clue.text: Unspecified number of streaming channels offering basic service

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase describing something stripped to the essentials

parts.note: N stands for an unspecified number in algebra
taken as written
rills are small streams, channels that water runs along

explanation.surface: A TV subscription advertising a vague number of streaming channels on its cheapest, most basic tier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Streaming channels' suggests TV services, but here it means little watercourses. N for an unknown number is a maths convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-frills business or product gives only the essentials without extras, which is exactly a basic level of service.

clue.text: Took a picture capturing wild animal

indicators.note: to capture is to hold inside, so the wanted letters sit within the preceding words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, the whole second word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A wildlife photographer snaps a shot of some animal on safari.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capturing' fits the photo story as catching on film, but it signals that the answer is held inside 'Took a picture'.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi is a forest-dwelling relative of the giraffe from central Africa, a genuinely wild creature.

clue.text: Farm animal close to river in the morning

parts.note: R is the standard abbreviation for river
a.m. marks times in the morning

explanation.surface: A sheep grazes by a riverbank early in the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to' reads as near the river, but it only joins definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A ram is a male sheep, kept on farms for breeding with the flock.

clue.text: Pub suitable for some dieters?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the nearby pub one regularly drinks at, in British usage
second meaning, read as two parts: low-calorie, spelt the way food labels shorten it

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain your 'local' is the pub nearest home. Split as LO-CAL it becomes the label on reduced-calorie food, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: British speakers call their regular neighbourhood pub their local, and lo-cal food suits people cutting calories.

clue.text: Old fighter in Asia struggling to keep spirit up

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards
to keep is to hold onto, so one set of letters holds another inside
something struggling is thrashing about, so these letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: taken as written, for rearranging
rum is a spirit, the alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: An old soldier in the Far East needs a drink to keep his morale up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' suggests morale but means a drink. The rearranged continent splits around the upturned drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Samurai were the hereditary warrior class of feudal Japan, so a samurai is a historical fighting man.

clue.text: Kind characters in variety performance

indicators.note: the letters, or characters, contained in a phrase are the ones wanted

parts.note: the end of the first word joins the start of the second

explanation.surface: Pleasant, good-natured performers appear in a variety show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind' looks like an adjective describing the characters, but it is a noun meaning sort. 'Characters' means letters, not cast members.
explanation.definitionFit: A type is a category or sort of thing, the same as a kind when grouping similar items.

clue.text: Spooner's advice for dog is so long

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so the initial sounds trade places

parts.note: a tip for a poodle is advice for a dog; swapping the P and T sounds gives the farewell

explanation.surface: Someone declares that the advice for a dog is far too long-winded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So long' looks like a complaint about length, but it is a goodbye. Toodle-pip is old-fashioned British slang for cheerio.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are casual ways of saying goodbye; toodle-pip is a jaunty, dated British farewell.

clue.text: Spotted horse that is in lead with extraordinary lad

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another means it is placed inside it

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
i.e. abbreviates the Latin id est, that is

indicators.note: extraordinary means out of the ordinary order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, for rearranging

explanation.surface: A patchy-coated horse is out in front at the races, ridden by a remarkable young jockey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' reads as being ahead in a race, but it is the metal, symbol Pb, which surrounds the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A piebald horse has irregular patches of black and white, so it is a horse with a spotted coat.

clue.text: Starts to prune around large maple tree

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, so take each word's first letter

parts.note: one opening letter from each of these four words

explanation.surface: A gardener begins cutting back the branches surrounding a big maple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maple tree' wants to be one unit, but 'maple' only donates its first letter and 'tree' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Palms are tropical trees with a tall unbranched trunk topped by large fan or feather leaves.

clue.text: She scores 100 initially on maths problem

definitions.note: a clause standing for 'one who scores', so a noun in effect

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so keep the first letter of each word it governs

parts.note: the first letter of each of these two words
a poser is a puzzling problem

explanation.surface: A student gets full marks on her first attempt at a maths problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scores 100' reads as a perfect test mark; really she writes musical scores, and 100 is the Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: A composer writes music; to score a film or piece is to compose its music, so a woman who scores is a composer.

clue.text: Republican backing amendment of crucial letter

indicators.note: to back something is to stand behind it, so this piece goes at the end
an amendment changes a text, so these letters are altered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, for rearranging
R abbreviates Republican

explanation.surface: A Republican politician supports a constitutional amendment in an important letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' sounds like political support but places R at the back. 'Amendment' fits US politics yet signals rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: A circular is a letter or notice sent out to many people at once, such as a mass mailing.

clue.text: Two churches hosting a very loud popular singer

indicators.note: a host takes guests in, so the outer letters hold the others inside

parts.note: CH is the usual abbreviation for church, taken twice
taken as written
ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud
something in fashion is in, or popular

explanation.surface: Two congregations welcome a booming pop star to perform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Popular singer' reads as a pop star, but 'popular' is wordplay and 'singer' alone is a songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: The chaffinch is a common European finch known for its cheerful song, so in crosswords it is a singer.

clue.text: One serving Whoppers in bar on the counter

indicators.note: counter means opposite in direction, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: a rail is a bar, as on a fence or towel rail

explanation.surface: A fast-food worker hands Burger King Whoppers across the bar counter.
explanation.walkthrough: Whopper is a Burger King burger, but a whopper is also a big lie. 'On the counter' sounds like a serving counter.
explanation.definitionFit: A whopper is a blatant lie, so someone dishing out whoppers is telling untruths.

clue.text: Search over a long period, with no end in sight

indicators.note: having no end means the final letter is missing, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: for ages means over a very long time

explanation.surface: Someone has been looking for something for a very long time, with no end to the hunt in sight.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one long phrase about a fruitless search, but 'Search' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To forage is to rummage around looking for food or supplies, a kind of searching.

clue.text: Aromatic herb and orange cooked with duck

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so these letters are reworked into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, for rearranging
a duck in cricket is a score of zero, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A recipe: duck à l'orange seasoned with a fragrant herb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' looks like the bird in the dish; in cricket, being out without scoring is a duck, a zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregano is a fragrant Mediterranean culinary herb of the mint family, used widely in Italian cooking.

clue.text: Left outside cold and agitated

indicators.note: being outside something means wrapping round it, so one piece surrounds another

parts.note: to have left a place is to have exited it
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone shut out in the cold becomes upset and restless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left outside' reads as abandoned out of doors; 'Left' is a verb meaning went out.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitated and excited both describe a stirred-up, unsettled emotional state.

clue.text: Hamper emptied out except last of fruit

indicators.note: out can mean disordered or wrong, so these letters are rearranged
except means leaving out, so a letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written, for rearranging

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, so only that letter is taken

parts.note: the final letter of this word, which is removed

explanation.surface: A picnic hamper has been emptied of everything except the last piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hamper' looks like a basket, but it is the verb. 'Last of' is part of the selection, not a separate indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: To hamper someone is to hinder or obstruct their progress, which is what impede means.

clue.text: Identity of small supernatural creature

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
an elf is a magical being of folklore

explanation.surface: Someone asks who exactly a tiny magical being is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small supernatural creature' reads as a single phrase, but 'small' gives its own letter.
explanation.definitionFit: One's self is one's individual identity, the essential being that makes a person distinct.

clue.text: Support man entertaining millions in boxing ring

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to take them in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: chap is informal British for a man
M abbreviates million

indicators.note: to box something is to enclose it, so the outer letters wrap around

parts.note: taken as written
a ring is round, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: A boxer's cornerman entertains millions of viewers from the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxing ring' looks like a sporting venue, but 'boxing' means enclosing and 'ring' is a circle shape.
explanation.definitionFit: To champion a cause or person is to argue for and back them, which is to support them.

clue.text: Son wearing fancy coat and tie

indicators.note: to wear something is to have it around you, so one piece goes inside another
fancy means elaborate or fanciful, so the letters are worked into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, for rearranging
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A boy dressed up in a smart jacket and necktie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy coat and tie' reads as formal wear; 'tie' is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascot is a broad neck scarf or cravat worn looped under the chin, a style of tie.

clue.text: Love and marriage not appropriate for everyone? That might cause some tears

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written as O

indicators.note: not means without, so the named letter is taken away

parts.note: a marriage is a union of two people
U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for all ages

explanation.surface: A reflection that love and marriage aren't for everybody, since they can end in tears.
explanation.walkthrough: The tears look like heartbreak; they come from chopping. U is the British 'universal' film rating.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting an onion releases an irritant gas that stings the eyes and makes the cook weep.

clue.text: Attractive model acting with me

indicators.note: to model is to shape or mould, so these letters are reshaped into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, for rearranging
taken as written, for rearranging

explanation.surface: A good-looking fashion model is appearing in a film alongside the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attractive model' reads as a glamorous person, but 'model' is a verb telling you to reshape the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnetic means drawing things or people towards it, literally with magnets or figuratively with charm.

clue.text: Beginning of short family film

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of this word
one's kin are one's relatives

explanation.surface: The opening scene of a brief family movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' looks like a movie; here it is a thin layer, as on custard or hot milk.
explanation.definitionFit: A film is a thin coating or layer, and a skin forms on the surface of liquids like that.

clue.text: Knight is returning with king

indicators.note: returning means going back the way one came, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: taken as written
R abbreviates the Latin rex, king

explanation.surface: A knight comes back from campaign alongside his monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: R for king comes from the Latin rex, as in royal signatures.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir is the title given to a knight, placed before his name, so it stands for a knighted man.

clue.text: My turn — quiet!

parts.note: your go is your turn in a game
sh is the sound used to ask for quiet

explanation.surface: A player at a board game insists it is their move and asks everyone to hush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My turn' reads as a possessive phrase, but 'My' is the exclamation of surprise and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild exclamations of surprise, as in 'My, what a view!' or 'Gosh, what a view!'

clue.text: Bring down other end somehow

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters can be put together in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, for rearranging
taken as written, for rearranging

explanation.surface: An instruction to lower the far end of something, by whatever means.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bring down' sounds like lowering an object; here it means toppling a ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: To dethrone a monarch is to remove them from power, which is to topple or overthrow them.
